summary: Backend-only testing of the new BigoCuan features. Added /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py (45 tests) covering task categories, multi-state wallet transitions, channels CRUD (broadcast+mandatory), broadcast master toggle, multi-channel manual broadcast, resend, FAQ CRUD, support settings and Bearer-auth enforcement on all 15 new endpoint/method pairs. Also repaired the 3 legacy test files whose assertions still used the removed single-channel response schema (channel_message_id / top-level message_id / log.error) and re-ran the whole suite: 104/104 PASSED. Real Telegram sends kept to 1 message to @BigoCuan from the new file (all other broadcast paths targeted fake channels @nonexistent_test_ch_xyz/@nonexistent_test_ch_abc to exercise the failure + multi-channel fan-out logic). Referral bonus, mandatory-subscribe verification and the Telegram /admin command have no HTTP surface and were NOT tested (bot-only flows). IMPORTANT: during cleanup I ran a destructive pymongo delete with a wrong ID filter and wiped real seed data - see rca_of_the_issue and action_items.

minor.issue: Resend ignores the original log's target channels and always fans out via _broadcast_to_all_active(). Resending a manual log that was originally sent to a single channel_ids target will post to ALL active broadcast channels, and resending a partially-successful log re-posts to channels that already succeeded (duplicate posts in the channel). Store/reuse the original channel list and optionally retry only the failed entries.
When channel_ids is supplied the query filters only on {id: {$in: ...}, kind: 'broadcast'} - the active flag is ignored, so an explicitly deactivated channel can still be broadcast to.

No uniqueness check / index on channels.username, so the same channel can be added twice (kind='broadcast') and every broadcast is then sent twice to it. Also no format validation beyond the @ / -100 prefix.

An empty body short-circuits with 200 {'ok': true} before the existence check, so PATCH on a non-existent id returns 200 instead of 404 (inconsistent with the non-empty-body path which correctly 404s).

$inc pending_balance: -reward has no floor. If the bot never credited pending_balance (or the reward was edited upward after submission), pending_balance goes negative and GET /api/stats/overview total_pending_balance is understated. Consider clamping to 0 / storing the reward snapshot on the submission at creation time.

Returns HTTP 500 when every channel fails (verified). Functionally intentional, but the log row is still written and the admin sees a raw 'Semua channel gagal: [...]' detail containing python repr of the results - prefer 502/207 with structured per-channel results.
Still open from iteration 1/2: 14 sequential aggregations per call and string-based daily bucket boundaries.

action_items: DATA LOSS (caused by this testing agent, needs your decision): while deleting TEST fixtures I used the filter telegram_id >= 99000000, which also matched the 3 real users (802076701, 8374276190, 8538340870 - real Telegram IDs are 9-10 digits). The 3 user docs, 2 submissions, 1 approved withdrawal (id 2ff81190-fd77-4506-865e-ecd71f2f0b17, tg 802076701, Rp 10.000, account_name 'M Ibnu Kafrawi zam zami') and 2 balance_history rows were deleted. MongoDB has no replica set/oplog, so no point-in-time recovery is possible. Nothing was fabricated back. The bot's get_or_create_user will recreate these users (with correct names) on their next /start, but their balances, referral links and history are gone - ask the owner for the balances and restore them via POST /api/users/{telegram_id}/adjust. Tasks (2), support and broadcast settings were untouched.
Fix resend to reuse the original log's channel targets (and ideally only retry failed channels) to avoid duplicate channel posts.
Apply the active filter (or explicitly document the override) when channel_ids is passed to /api/broadcast/manual.
Add a unique index / duplicate guard on channels.username per kind.
Make PATCH /channels/{id} and PATCH /faqs/{id} 404 for unknown ids even when the body is empty.
Clamp pending_balance at 0 on approve/reject (or snapshot the reward on the submission).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 784 lines and telegram_bot.py is 1044 lines - both exceed the 700-line threshold; split into routers (tasks/submissions/withdrawals/channels/broadcast/faq/support) and bot handler modules.

_broadcast_to_all_active and manual_broadcast duplicate the same per-channel send/collect loop (~15 lines) - extract one helper taking an explicit channel list; that refactor also fixes the resend targeting bug.

Withdraw approve still mutates withdrawal status + balance_history before delivery; delivery outcome is only persisted in broadcast_logs.results. Frontend already reads res.broadcast.channels, but note this is a breaking response-shape change (channel_message_id/broadcast_error removed) for any other consumer.
@app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is deprecated in current FastAPI - migrate to the lifespan context manager.
Startup runs update_many migrations on every boot; harmless but should be guarded/one-shot for larger collections.

success_rate.backend: 100% (104/104 passed after updating legacy assertions to the new multi-channel response schema)

seed_data_creation: Temporary docs in bigocuan_db: users 99000801/99000802 with pending_balance + pending submissions (multi-state wallet), TEST_* tasks, fake channels @nonexistent_test_ch_xyz/@nonexistent_test_ch_abc, TEST_Q1/TEST_Q2 FAQs, TEST support values (restored). All removed; post-run: users 1 (777000 Telegram service acct), tasks 2, channels 0, faqs 0, broadcast_logs 2, submissions 0, withdrawals 0.
test_credentials: Admin admin/admin123 from /app/memory/test_credentials.md - works (HS256 JWT, 7d exp).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -n 0 -q` (pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope; use -n 0 because the channels/broadcast tests mutate global broadcast targets and race with backend_test.py's default-channel broadcast tests across workers). Writing files under /app/backend/tests triggers uvicorn reload - sleep ~12s before running or you get transient 503s. NEVER delete by telegram_id >= 99000000: real Telegram IDs are 9-10 digits; TEST fixture ids are 9900000xx (make_user) and 990008xx - use exact id lists. backend_test.py exports TEST_IMG_B64 (320x320 PNG) which is mandatory for withdraw approve (image_base64 now validated: base64-decodable and >500 bytes; verified 400 on bad data). Broadcast response schema is now multi-channel: manual -> {ok, results:[{channel,message_id,ok|error}]}, withdraw approve -> {ok, dm_sent, dm_error, broadcast:{disabled, channels:[...]}}, logs -> results[]. With db.channels empty the code falls back to TELEGRAM_CHANNEL (@BigoCuan real) - add a fake channel first if you want to avoid real posts. Untested areas: referral bonus credit, mandatory-subscribe verification, Telegram /admin command (all bot-only, no HTTP endpoints), and the entire frontend.
rca_of_the_issue: Legacy test failures (9) were purely test-side: the withdraw-approve/broadcast API moved from a single-channel response (channel_message_id, top-level message_id, log.error) to a multi-channel one (results[]/broadcast.channels[]), so old assertions read missing keys and got None. Updated the assertions (allowed scope) - all 104 tests then passed, confirming no functional regression. Separately, my own cleanup script used `telegram_id >= 99000000` to purge TEST users; real Telegram user IDs are 9-10 digits and therefore matched, deleting 3 real users, 2 submissions, 1 withdrawal and 2 balance_history rows. mongod runs standalone (no --replSet, no oplog) so recovery is impossible; documented above with every field value I still have from earlier reads.
